Subject: Seed/backfill plan + rerank acceptance — pilot → prod transition

Hi Jill / BrightMart team,

Thanks again for the productive pilot. We validated the reranker on the 10k test set and saw a 7.8% lift in NDCG@10 with the seeded embeddings/priming approach. Your success manager (Marissa) and our infra lead (Ben) are looped for execution.

Quick summary of what we need to move from pilot to production: 
- Seed/backfill strategy for historical content (approx 2.4M documents)
- Vector DB choice and backfill approach (bulk + incremental)
- Rerank smoke/eval criteria and acceptance gates
- Cutover schedule and rollback plan

I've attached a short index-backfill-plan.xlsx and a CSV sample of seed IDs (seed_ids.csv). Also included a one-page rerank-eval-criteria.md for acceptance. Please review and confirm a preferred 2-week window for an initial backfill (we can do staggered waves).

Proposed next steps:
1) BrightMart to confirm SLA for backfill window and whether the export can be staged into our S3 bucket.
2) Redwood to provide a detailed backfill runbook and required IAM roles.
3) Schedule a 45-min technical sync (Ben + Karthik + BrightMart infra) this week.

Can you confirm availability for an infra sync Thu or Fri PST?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0198

Jill — thanks for the quick reply, and good questions. Short answers first: 
1) Peak GPU estimate: for a bulk backfill of 2.4M docs with our recommended quantized float16 pipeline, expect ~120 GPU-hours (NVIDIA A10 equivalent) if run as a single wave; staggered waves reduce peak.
2) Yes — we recommend a shadow index approach for the rerank smoke and traffic mirroring for a short validation period (48–72 hours) before cutting.

More details and constraints: 
- Retention: 7 days for the pre-signed S3 export is fine. We'll provide a presigned upload URL and an expiration time in the runbook.
- Delta flow: we can wire the nightly ETL; Redwood will consume the delta feed (JSONL) and run incremental embedding jobs. We will provide sample manifest format.

I've attached the rerank-eval-criteria.md that lists gate metrics (NDCG thresholds, MRR delta, and a qualitative human review pass for template-heavy pages). If acceptable, we'll schedule the infra sync Thu 14:00 PST. Ben and Karthik will lead the technical discussion.

Naomi

Folks — following up with a technical note ahead of Thu's sync. 

Key considerations for backfill and vectorstore selection: 
- Throughput vs cost: If BrightMart prefers lower wall-clock time, we suggest parallelized A10 clusters and a single-wave backfill. If cost is a concern, staggered waves with aggressive batching and prefix caching reduce unit cost substantially.
- Storage format: We recommend writing embeddings as 32-bit floats to S3 then compressing with zstd for transfer; Redwood's ingestion supports float16/float32 and will quantize as needed on ingest.
- Vector DB: Both Pinecone and an open-source vectorstore on managed PostgreSQL (pgvector) are compatible. For BrightMart's 2.4M vectors, we recommend starting with a managed vector DB for indexing speed; fallback to pgvector for cost-sensitive tiers.
- Backfill orchestration: We'll provide a runbook that stages: export → validate manifest → upload → dry-run ingest (sample 10k) → bulk ingest → post-index checks. Dry-run is required.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Duplicate IDs: we will run a de-dup step and provide a reconciliation report; BrightMart should include a primary key in the manifest.
- Rerank regression: run the reranker in shadow with traffic mirroring for 48 hours and run the rerank-eval-criteria.md checks; hold cutover until gates pass.

Attaching a brief index-backfill-plan.xlsx and the expected manifest schema in the drive link Naomi shared.

Ben Carter
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
